title: Why Blue LEDs Need More Voltage

segments.text: Why does a blue chip need extra push?
In an LED, electrons recombine with holes and emit photons—a process called electroluminescence.
The photon’s color matches the semiconductor’s band‑gap energy, and shorter‑wavelength blue light requires a larger band gap than red, so a higher forward voltage is needed.
Because the semiconductor material has a high index of refraction, special optical coatings and the shape of the die are used to let light escape efficiently.
These design features let the blue chip convert electricity into bright blue light with good efficiency.
